newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil gains due to shortage, loading delay.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil gains due to shortage, loading delay.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel barges gained on Tuesday on the contined shortage of prompt material from refiners and loading delays at two key storage sites, traders said.

High sulphur barges traded at $96 a tonne after four deals at $95.50 fob ARA, or up to $2 higher than Monday trades. Later offers were in the $96.50/$97 range and there was unconfirmed talk of a trade at $97.

"There's nothing in storage with the majors. The problem is that we don't have a lot in storage from refiners and under normal circumstances, what refiners produce is not enough to cover the market anyway," one trader said.
"Loading is very slack also," he added. Traders said that there were loading delays at two key independent storage sites.
An independent trader said that with barge prices at these levels he will sell six cargoes of Russian M-100 cracked he is receiving soon straight into the barge market.
"I will be very happy to flood them with 200,000 tonnes. In the next few days I will be landing 210,000 tonnes, six cargoes, arriving into Rotterdam," he said.

High sulphur cargoes were also reportedly a little stronger, with talk of a Russian cracked M-100 fetching two means +$2 compared with an asking price of $1.50 over the two means quote on Monday for a similar cargo.
Traders said the 15,000-tonne cargo was picked up by a major from a trader.
Russian high-sulphur straight-run was also offered stronger.

Traders said two E-4s were on offer at a strong three means plus $5, or $2 up on last done, but some doubted they would fetch that figure. Two M-40s were at two means plus $4, or $1 higher than earlier in the day. Shipping sources said an independent trader was looking for 40-80,000 tonnes of high sulphur straight-run out of Ventspils and Tallin for August 15-20 loading to go to the U.K., the Mediterranean or Trans-Atlantic.
